answer: Concrete defense: each seat must deliver nectar in numbered jars whose Brix reading matches its own pollinator garden bloom log. Every jar is sealed by a tide logger bolted to a registered reef flat, so the stamp time can only come from that flat's real tidal calendar. Rented nectar fails the Brix-to-bloom match, and two seats sharing a reef flat emit overlapping tide series, exposing one operator behind many keys. An attacker thus needs a garden, a reef flat and a logger per identity, plus weekly harvests and forfeiture on first mismatch; cost scales with fake seats, payout does not.
